slides.title: Entertainment and Media
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 6 English, Unit 8: Entertainment and Media. In today's world, entertainment is everywhere. We watch films and documentaries on screens, listen to podcasts and radio shows, follow stories through books and graphic novels, and even create our own content. But how much do we think about the media we consume? How does a film tell a story? What makes a documentary different from a drama? Why do some adverts stay in our minds long after we have seen them? In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and understand texts about entertainment and media, including film, television, and storytelling traditions.
Use participle adjectives correctly, choosing between the -ed form (how someone feels) and the -ing form (what causes the feeling).
Form sentences in the past simple passive to describe events in film and history (e.g. "The documentary was filmed in Mogadishu").
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand texts about entertainment and media, including film, television, and storytelling traditions. You will also use participle adjectives correctly, choosing between the -ed form (how someone feels) and the -ing form (what causes the feeling). You will also form sentences in the past simple passive to describe events in film and history (e.g. "The documentary was filmed in Mogadishu"). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: rehearsal, apprentice, eternal, revival, ancestral, classical. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Screens, Stories, and the Art of Telling Tales
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Why Entertainment Matters and Screens, Stories, and the Art of Telling Tales. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Participle Adjectives (-ed and -ing)
bullets: Participle adjectives come from verbs but describe nouns. The -ed form tells us how a person feels; the -ing form tells us what causes the feeling.
slides.narration: The first language focus is Participle Adjectives (-ed and -ing). Participle adjectives come from verbs but describe nouns. The -ed form tells us how a person feels; the -ing form tells us what causes the feeling. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Media Habits Interview. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
